The test image shows a soybean leaf with brown necrotic tissue along the leaf margin/edge, with a yellowish-green transition zone between dead and healthy tissue. Some tissue appears to have fallen out giving a ragged edge. This is a **leaf** symptom.

Top candidates from the 16 leaf classes based on marginal necrosis: Bacterial_Blight, Septoria_brown_spot, Bacterial_Pustule, Anthracnose, Phyllosticta_leaf_spot, Frogeye_leaf_spot, Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus, Downy_mildew.

Let me view reference images one at a time, one per class first.
Bacterial_Blight reference shows scattered small angular yellow-brown spots, not the large marginal necrosis in the test image. Not a strong match.
Septoria shows small dark brown spots on yellowed leaves, not marginal necrosis. Not a match.
Anthracnose shows shepherd's crook and curled leaf with spots. Not the same pattern.
This is a strong match. Phyllosticta shows a tan/brown lesion with dark margins at the leaf edge, very similar to the test image. Let me continue checking other candidates.
SVN virus shows yellow spots along veins progressing to brown necrotic lesions. The pattern is different from the test image's marginal necrosis.
Downy mildew shows scattered pale yellow spots across the leaf surface. Very different from the test image.

Frogeye leaf spot shows small circular gray spots with reddish-brown borders scattered across the leaf. Very different from the test image.

Now let me view a second Phyllosticta reference to confirm the match.

This is an excellent match. The second Phyllosticta reference shows the same pattern as the test image: a tan/brown irregular necrotic lesion at the leaf margin with a yellowish-green transition zone and dark margins, on an otherwise green leaf. The visual similarity is very strong.

Key matching features:
- Irregularly shaped tan/brownish lesion at the leaf edge
- Yellowish-green margin between healthy green tissue and the brown necrotic area
- Dark purplish border around the lesion
- Otherwise green leaf
- Leaf appears to be from the lower canopy (consistent with Phyllosticta description of "cool, moist conditions" in lower canopy)

All other candidates (Bacterial_Blight, Septoria, Anthracnose, SVN virus, Downy mildew, Frogeye) showed distinctly different patterns.
